name: IvanSnezhok/air-raid-forecast-ua
type: repo (student / cohort peer project, same course), with a live GitHub Actions pipeline, a GitHub Pages / FastAPI web app, and a separate raion-level layer
year: 2026 (created 2026-10-11, last push 2026-10-17, i.e. work continued after the 12 Oct deadline; about 126 commits)
authors: IvanSnezhok (single human author); 'claude' is listed as a co-contributor (AI-assisted, several parallel Claude threads per docs/PROCESS_uk.md)
peer_review_status: student repo, self-reported results; not peer reviewed
target_type: Both, reported side by side: 'active' (state: alert active at any moment of hour T+h) and 'onset' (a new alert starts within [T, T+h)). The author explicitly says the active target is inflated by running alerts and added onset after reviewing related work. However the onset target is NOT restricted to rows clear at T, so it is a hybrid: in the volunteer file any new 'alert' post restarts the oblast alert, so an 'onset' can occur while an alert is running.
target_definition: Origins at top of hour T (UTC; live pipeline also at any minute, every 10 min). Horizons h in {1, 2, 3, 6} hours, one model per target and horizon. active_h: region has an alert at any moment of [T+(h-1)h, T+h h). onset_h: max of hourly alert-start indicators over [T, T+h) (src/airraid/features.py labels()). Labels NaN beyond the data end. Test base rates: active 33%; onset 23% / 39% / 50% / 67% for h = 1/2/3/6.
spatial_unit: oblast (23 oblasts + Kyiv City = 24 units, Luhansk excluded); a separate raion layer forecasts 119 units (118 raions + Kyiv City)
at_risk_masking: No. Onset rows where the oblast is already under alert at T are neither dropped from training nor from scoring (no mask in features.py / run.py / evaluate.py). This inflates the onset base rate (23% at 1h) and the score, and makes the onset result not directly comparable to our masked onset target. [uncertain: checked by code reading of labels() and grep, not by running]
data_sources: Vadimkin/ukrainian-air-raid-sirens-dataset volunteer (eTryvoga) file, 116k oblast-level alerts 2022-02-25 to 2026-10-11 04:36 UTC (training and headline test). Official raion-level file of the same repo used for the raion layer (Dec 2025 - 2026-09-07) and for the live-definition check. alerts.in.ua API (live polls every 10 min plus daily history pull, backfilled from 2026-09-11) stored in a point-in-time store on the 'live-data' branch. Telegram: kpszsu (Air Force), deraketaua, monitorwarr, war_monitor via public web preview, complete from 2025-01-01, stored on a 'text-data' branch. RSS and GDELT news collected but not used. Kaggle 'Massive Missile Attacks' only to validate the morning-summary parser.
data_source_variant: Volunteer file (NOT official) for the oblast model, oblast-level only, snapshot 2026-10-11. The official file was rejected because it froze on 2026-09-07 and changed meaning in Dec 2025 (raion-level declarations). Live alerts.in.ua records of any level (oblast/raion/hromada/city) are replayed into oblast intervals by a measured rule (latest activation starts the oblast alert, any all-clear ends it, 1h expiry with no new activation). Raion layer uses the official file (union of hromada/city records into their raion; oblast records to all raions) plus alerts.in.ua.
preprocessing: src/airraid/data.py: Luhansk dropped, zero-length records dropped, alerts capped at 12h (missed all-clears; e.g. 177h in Chernivtsi), cap depends only on elapsed time so it is causal. Naive imputed ends (naive=True, start+30 min, about 5%) kept as-is. Overlapping intervals merged into a minute grid. No explicit deduplication step documented for the volunteer file [uncertain]. No gap masking documented for the volunteer file. Live: oblast intervals from alerts.in.ua via a measured replay rule with 1h expiry, chosen on a selection period (Jan-Apr 2026) by downstream Brier, so month-long frontline hromada alerts never make an oblast active (functionally similar to our D-020 standing-alert cap). Text archive keeps first-seen text, publish time and edit flags; posts already edited when first seen count only from first sighting.
known_label_artefacts: (1) Naive 30-min ends (about 5% of volunteer records): kept as labels; the leak documented by Dashulya-coder (naive=True implies no new activation for >= 3h) is NOT discussed, and duration / time-since-end features may read naive ends [uncertain]. (2) Long records / missed all-clears: 12h causal cap. (3) Standing frontline hromada alerts in alerts.in.ua (Kharkivska hromada open since 2026-03-10): first live merge treated them as whole-oblast alerts and trained on them, producing active 0.999 / onset 0.000 forecasts for Kharkivska and Dnipropetrovska; fixed by the 1h-expiry replay rule and by never training on live data, with regression tests (tests/test_live_alerts.py). (4) Official-file staleness and the Dec 2025 raion reform: avoided by using the volunteer file. (5) Volunteer starts only partly match official sirens: 87% of volunteer ends coincide with an official all-clear, only 49% of starts with an activation (channel also posts threat notices). (6) 7-12 Sep 2026 gap: noted for the raion layer. (7) Duplicates: not mentioned for the volunteer file. (8) Telegram edits: 12,465 of 130,989 posts dropped as edited-before-first-seen.
model_family: LightGBM (pooled over regions, one per target x horizon) as main model; also logistic regression (last 12 months), LightGBM without spatial features (ablation), lightgbm_cov (Telegram-period rows only) and lightgbm_text (+ Telegram). Baselines: 28-day same-hour climatology, raw persistence, 'Markov' persistence (P(event | region, alert running now) fitted on train). A survival-hazard model was tried separately and lost by 0.002-0.005 Brier. Raion layer: LightGBM 'current state' and '+28-day history', oblast probability, oblast x share. Live: Platt recalibration from verified forecasts.
features: Own state: alert running now, elapsed duration, minutes since last end, starts in last 6h/24h/7d. Own history: share of each of the last 24 hours under alert, share of last 24h/7d/28d. National: number of regions under alert now, nationwide starts in last 1h/3h, national share of last 24h. Spatial (learned lead-lag): now__<region> and lag1__<region> for each of the 24 regions (state now and in the last hour), instead of a hand-coded neighbour map; the ablation without them scored the same. Calendar: Kyiv-local hour and weekday of the target hour; same-hour climatology over 7/28 days (active and onset versions). Telegram (lightgbm_text only): posts naming the oblast in last 30/60/180 min total and by threat (drones, missiles, ballistic, KABs, all-clear), minutes since oblast last named with a threat, nationwide threat posts by class, number of oblasts named in last hour, strategic bomber / MiG-31K take-offs, ballistic threats, launch reports, 'massed attack' wording, drone/missile counts of the latest morning summary; NaN plus tg_covered=0 outside archive coverage. Top features by gain: onset climatology, starts in last 7d, hour climatology, alert running now, elapsed time. Text features took 16% of gain.
external_feature_timing: Carefully handled. Each post has an available_at: publish time if not edited when first seen; first sighting if already edited (so backfilled edited posts are unusable in history); RSS news at first sighting; GDELT at crawl time (seendate), never claimed publish time. Features use a strict '< T' window. Morning launch counts are taken from the Air Force summaries with their publish time (not from Kaggle, whose row timing is unknown). A deliberately leaky 'permissive' variant (all posts at publish time with final text) bounds the edit-rule effect: at most 0.3-0.4 points of Brier improvement. Timing analysis: Air Force posts naming an oblast are at background rate until ~1h before onset, +15-25% in the last hour, and double only in the last 15 min, i.e. mostly concurrent rather than leading signals.
ablation_design: Yes, time-fair. lightgbm_cov (history only) and lightgbm_text (history + Telegram) are trained on exactly the same rows (origins from 2025-01-03, the archive start, to each fold start minus 6h embargo), same weekly folds, trees chosen on the validation month for each separately; delta Brier with a 95% day-block bootstrap CI. This avoids the common confound of comparing a text model trained on a short window against a history model trained on all data. Also a spatial ablation (lightgbm_no_spatial vs lightgbm) and channel ablation (kpszsu only vs all 4 channels) on validation, and an edit-rule sensitivity run. The live serving rule (text model where it beat history-only on validation) was fixed before looking at the test.
split_scheme: Chronological walk-forward. Validation month 2026-08-15 to 2026-09-12 for model selection (training window 3/6/12/24 months/all, number of trees by early stopping). Test: origins 2026-09-12 23:00 to 2026-10-10 23:00 UTC, four weekly folds; every model refit on data up to each fold start. Embargo: training origins stop 6h (max horizon) before the first evaluated origin. Raion layer: same protocol on the official file's last 4 weeks (2026-08-09 to 09-06) and on alerts.in.ua labels (2026-09-13 to 10-10). Live: daily refit plus 10-min forecasts.
metrics: Brier score, Brier skill score vs 28-day same-hour climatology, log loss, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, reliability diagrams, per-region skill and within-region AUC. Live verification: Brier vs climatology over 24h/7d/all time, hit rate, recall and false alarm ratio at p >= 0.5.
unit_of_metric: Pooled over regions for headline numbers; per-region skill and within-region AUC reported separately (onset-3h within-region AUC 0.52-0.74, median about 0.6), with the explicit note that pooled AUC flatters the model.
baseline_strength: Climatology (28-day same-hour, the skill reference, effectively a rolling recent-rate by hour), raw persistence, calibrated 'Markov' persistence, logistic regression. Onset results: LightGBM beats climatology by only +5% / +4% / +3% / +3% Brier skill (h = 1/2/3/6); logistic regression is within 0.003 Brier. Persistence is worse than climatology at every horizon; Markov persistence helps only at 1h for active. No CI reported for the model vs climatology gain (only for text vs no-text). Active-1h skill +28% is mostly 'alert running now'.
calibration: Reliability diagrams on the test (reports/figures/reliability.png, text_reliability.png); author reports curves on the diagonal and reliability error <= 0.0012 for both text and no-text models. No post-hoc calibration in evaluation. Live: Platt map p = sigmoid(a + b logit(p_raw)) fitted per target x horizon on the last 7 days of verified forecasts, shrunk toward identity (ridge 20*h pseudo region-hours), weighted to one row per region x clock hour, served only if it improves Brier by >= 1% on a held-out check day; applied point-in-time (as_of=T), tested in tests/test_recalibration.py. A sub-hour backtest checks calibration at :00 vs :10..:50 origins.
calibration_under_drift: Partially. Test lies after a known regime shift (2026: twice as many, shorter alerts); weekly refit absorbs some drift. No explicit calibration-in-the-large (mean predicted vs observed) table per week or per group in the README [uncertain]. The live recalibration layer is the drift response. On the raion layer the author notes smaller gains on the latest weeks (active base rate 39% vs 28%). The live-rule vs volunteer-state mismatch is measured: active-1h Brier 0.19 vs 0.14.
uncertainty_of_gain: Day-block bootstrap 95% CI only for the Telegram ablation delta (text minus cov). Results: interval excludes zero only for onset 2h (-0.0018 [-0.0037, -0.0001]); onset 1h touches zero (-0.0012 [-0.0024, +0.0000]); others include zero. No CI or DM test for the main model vs climatology.
regime_coverage: Test 2026-09-12 to 10-10 is entirely after the Sep-2026 yellow/red reform, but as seen through the volunteer eTryvoga channel (oblast-level), so the reform is not analysed as such [uncertain]. Training spans 2022-03 onward and includes the Jan-2025 drone surge and the Dec-2025 raion reform; the Dec-2025 reform was the stated reason to reject the official file for the oblast model. Validation preferred long windows (all history or 24 months) despite the 2026 shift.
leakage_handling: Strong and well tested. (1) Construction: features use minutes strictly before T plus 'alert running at T and its elapsed time'; end of a running alert never used. (2) Truncation test (tests/test_leakage.py): features rebuilt from data truncated at T must equal full-data features; negative controls: injected lag-0 feature and 'minutes since last end' using the running alert's end both make it fail. (3) Sub-hour truncation test at :10/:23/:40/:50 origins with a mutation test. (4) Label test: wiping history before T must not change labels. (5) Text leakage tests on a synthetic archive (posts at T, T+1, T+60 change nothing, T-1 does; '<= T' mutation fails; edited-when-first-seen rule; live path equals evaluation path), plus a real-archive truncation check at 25 origins. (6) Raion leakage tests with two injected leaks. (7) 6h embargo at every fold. (8) Live: never train on live data; store rows used only as known at T. (9) Found and fixed a label-as-feature bug (validation Brier 0.0000, AUC 1.0) that the truncation test missed; added a guard that aborts if validation AUC > 0.995. Missed or limits: no at-risk mask for onset; naive 30-min ends not analysed as a leak channel; the 12h cap and live 1h expiry are causal by construction.
test_window_hygiene: Moderate. Model selection on the validation month only; Telegram serving rule fixed on validation before looking at the test. But the test was evaluated several times during a one-day build (the first run was lost to a 30-min job limit; Telegram ablation, sensitivity runs and the raion layer were run on the same test weeks after the main results were known), and there is no pre-registration or test lock [uncertain]. The oblast model's test labels also come from the volunteer channel, not the official file.
headline_results: Oblast, test 2026-09-12..10-10, about 16k forecasts per target x horizon. Onset Brier (skill vs 28-day climatology): LightGBM 0.146 (+5%), 0.176 (+4%), 0.176 (+3%), 0.132 (+3%) at h = 1/2/3/6; climatology 0.153/0.183/0.182/0.137; logistic 0.149/0.180/0.180/0.136; persistence 0.311-0.363 (much worse). Active: LightGBM 0.132 (+28%) at 1h, then +2 to +4%. ROC-AUC onset 0.78/0.80/0.81/0.86 (pooled); within-region onset-3h AUC 0.52-0.74, median about 0.6; per-region skill from -4% (Zaporizhzhia) to +10% (Ternopil). Spatial (learned lead-lag) features gave no gain. Telegram: onset 1-3h Brier -0.0012/-0.0018/-0.0017 (skill +4.7->+5.5, +4.1->+5.1, +3.9->+4.9), AUC +0.006-0.009; CI excludes zero only at onset 2h; nearly all from the Air Force channel. Raion layer: raion model beats raion climatology (onset 1h +16% on official file, +10% on alerts.in.ua labels), while the oblast probability used as-is is worse than raion climatology (-19% to -56%). Beats naive persistence clearly; beats climatology only modestly; no recent-rate or calibrated-persistence-at-risk baseline in our sense.
code_available: Yes, public on GitHub, no license; Python package (src/airraid, src/airraid_app), extensive pytest suite, GitHub Actions pipeline (10-min poll, daily train), data on orphan branches live-data and text-data; actively maintained as of 2026-10-17.
takeaways_for_project: (1) Learned lead-lag via per-region now/lag1 state columns did NOT beat national counts plus own history; supports keeping our simple neighbours_active + national_active_count features and not adding a 24-column region-state block. (2) Their onset skill over a same-hour 28-day climatology is only +3-5%, even WITHOUT at-risk masking; expect our masked onset BSS vs the rolling recent-rate baseline (D-021) to be small or negative, and report it honestly. (3) Pooled vs within-region AUC gap (0.78 pooled vs ~0.6 within) confirms our requirement to report both. (4) Their live-rule finding (1h expiry after the latest activation, any-level all-clear ends) is an empirical cousin of our D-020 24h standing cap and D-027 'keep open alerts'; useful evidence that long frontline hromada alerts must be capped causally for the alerts.in.ua exploratory section. (5) The label-as-feature bug that passed the truncation test is a concrete reason to keep our leakage test's negative control (CLAUDE.md) and to add an AUC>0.995 abort guard. (6) Their 6h embargo equals our purge rule; our purge is horizon-specific. (7) Telegram time-fair ablation design (same rows, same folds, bootstrap CI) is the right template if external features are ever considered, but they are out of our scope and add ~1% Brier. (8) Their results are on volunteer data; never compare their numbers to ours (official data, masked onset) directly.
best_practices: Adopt: truncation test with injected-leak negative controls (lag-0 and running-alert end); a separate label test; a sanity guard that aborts on implausibly perfect validation AUC; horizon-sized embargo at every refit; time-fair ablations (same rows and folds for with/without feature sets) with day-block bootstrap CIs; reporting within-unit AUC and per-unit skill alongside pooled numbers; honest 'what this means' sections; measuring a live definition against training labels before using it; point-in-time store with first_seen_at for any live data; available_at per external record and never trusting claimed publish times. Avoid: onset target without at-risk masking (inflated base rate, not a true onset estimand); scoring the same test weeks repeatedly while adding components; no CI on the headline gain vs the reference baseline; using naive 30-min ends without analysing their leak; mixing sources (volunteer training, alerts.in.ua live state) without a scored transfer check (they did measure it, which is good); large scope (web app, raions, Telegram) in a one-day build at the expense of a locked test.
